note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
“But know that the Lord hath set apart him that is godly for himself: the Lord will hear when I call unto him.” Peter shows the other side of being set apart: “The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished”. The same Most High who sets apart the godly also knows how to deliver them.

This ties to the class the bishop taught about being sealed. The Most High knows how to keep those meant for the kingdom and deliver them out of their temptations. But none of us can be certain we are meant for the kingdom, so do not lose your crown, and do not let anybody lead you or cause you to lose it, because only you can do that.

precepts.text: The Most High has commanded no man to do wickedly and has given no man licence to sin, so whatever you are going through does not give you the right to sin.
precepts.point: Stand in awe, and sin not; commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah. Be angry but sin not; no matter what you are going through, the Most High does not give you the right to sin.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
“Stand in awe, and sin not”. Be angry, but sin not. Ecclesiasticus closes the door on every excuse: “He hath commanded no man to do wickedly, neither hath he given any man licence to sin.” The Most High has commanded no man to do wickedly and has given no man licence to sin, so whatever you are going through does not give you the right to sin.

Instead, “commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still.” No matter what you are going through, the Most High has not given you the right to sin.

precepts.text: He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough, and he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering, which was a sacrifice.
precepts.point: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord. The sacrifice of righteousness today is keeping the law and presenting your body a living sacrifice.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
“Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord.” What is the sacrifice of righteousness today? “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.” The peace offering was a sacrifice; keeping the law and taking heed to the commandment is offering it. “He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise.”

So the sacrifice of righteousness today is keeping the law. He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough, and that is how we offer it and put our trust in the Lord.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. This means the dietary laws are not done away, the dress code is not done away, and we still keep the ceremonial laws when we come back into the knowledge of who we are.
precepts.point: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord. The sacrifice of righteousness today is keeping the law and presenting your body a living sacrifice.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
The sacrifice of righteousness today is also our own body: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Presenting your body a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable, is the sacrifice David speaks of.

That means the dietary laws are not done away, the dress code is not done away, and we still keep the ceremonial laws when we come back into the knowledge of who we are. Keeping the law in the body is our reasonable service.

precepts.text: He hath not dealt with us after our sins, nor rewarded us according to our iniquities; as far as the east is from the west, so far hath He removed our transgressions from us. Even though believing in white Jesus, Allah, or Buddha or keeping your birthday was idolatry punishable by death, He is forever merciful to them that fear Him by keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord. The sacrifice of righteousness today is keeping the law and presenting your body a living sacrifice.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
We offer the sacrifices of righteousness and put our trust in the Lord, and this is why: “He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities. For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.”

Believing in white Jesus, Allah or Buddha, or keeping your birthday, was idolatry punishable by death. Yet he has not rewarded us according to those iniquities. “Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.” He is for ever merciful to them that fear him, and fearing him is keeping the commandments: the sacrifice of righteousness.

precepts.text: Wherefore ye shall do my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them; and ye shall dwell in the land in safety. Safety in the land is tied directly to doing the statutes and judgments.
precepts.point: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep; for thou, Lord, only makest me to dwell in safety. Safety comes from the Most High, and it comes by keeping His statutes and judgments.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
“I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety.” Where does that safety come from? “Wherefore ye shall do my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them; and ye shall dwell in the land in safety.” Safety in the land is tied directly to doing the statutes and judgments.

Safety comes from the Most High, and it comes by keeping his statutes and judgments. That is why David can lie down in peace and sleep: the Lord only makes him dwell in safety, and he dwells in safety because he keeps the law.

precepts.text: If our forefathers had walked in the way of the Most High they would have dwelled in peace forever, which shows we are the ones under the curses, because right now we are not living in a time of peace.
precepts.point: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep; for thou, Lord, only makest me to dwell in safety. Safety comes from the Most High, and it comes by keeping His statutes and judgments.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
“Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom. For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou shouldest have dwelled in peace for ever.” If our forefathers had walked in the way of the Most High, they would have dwelled in peace for ever. They did not, and that shows we are the ones under the curses, because right now we are not living in a time of peace.

David lay down in peace and slept because the Lord made him dwell in safety, and that safety is tied to doing the statutes and judgments. Forsake the fountain of wisdom, and the peace goes with it. “There be many that say, Who will shew us any good?” The good, the gladness in the heart greater than the increase of corn and wine, comes when the Most High lifts up the light of his countenance upon us, and that is by walking in his way.

precepts.text: Stand in awe and sin not, commune with your own heart upon your bed and be still; know yourself in your alone time and ask what you can do.
precepts.point: Who can understand his errors? Cleanse thou me from secret faults. This should be your reason to be in this walk, not to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment; work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.” Stand in awe and sin not; commune with your own heart upon your bed and be still.

Know yourself in your alone time and ask what you can do. That is how you get at the secret faults: not to appear righteous before others, but to be cleansed where only God sees.

precepts.text: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness and trust in the Most High; the light of His countenance puts gladness in the heart more than corn and wine increase.
precepts.point: The health of the countenance ties to a merry heart. You can always tell when someone carries something heavy; a broken spirit shows on the face. If you truly pay attention to somebody, you can tell when things are not going well with them.

note.label: Psalm 43: Send Out Thy Light and Thy Truth

precepts.why:
“Then will I go unto the altar of God, unto God my exceeding joy”. Psalm 4 shows what is offered at that altar and what comes of it: “Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord.” Many say “Who will shew us any good?”, and the answer is “Lord, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us. Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased.”

That is why the altar is called his exceeding joy. The light of his countenance puts gladness in the heart more than corn and wine increase, and the one who trusts in him can say “I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety.” So when the soul is cast down and disquieted, the answer is “hope in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance”.

precepts.text: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, the law of sacrifice Paul kept blamelessly.
precepts.point: Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
“Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord.” The sacrifices of righteousness are the law of sacrifice, and that is the law Paul kept blamelessly, touching the righteousness which is in the law.

Paul had to give this resume again and again because he came up under Christ and not under the apostles. A man blameless in the law of sacrifice was now preaching in the synagogues that Christ is the Son of God.
